evals.name: cold-vague-request
evals.prompt: write me a plan for adding caching to my api, its getting slow
evals.expected_output: Does NOT produce a plan. Inspects the repository first, then identifies the key decisions that remain unresolved (which layer to cache, cache store, TTL/invalidation strategy, which endpoints, correctness constraints on the money path) and returns to discussion with concrete questions, ideally with recommendations attached.

evals.name: settled-discussion-with-open-item
evals.prompt:
ok so following up on everything we just went through, recapping it all in one place so its not spread across the thread:

we're pulling the order-total calculation out of orderService into its own thing. decided: new pricing/ module, pure functions only, no db access inside it — the repositories stay the only thing that touches postgres, same layering rule as the rest of the repo. we keep the existing OrderTotal shape as the return type so nothing downstream has to change.

the discount rules become a lookup table instead of the if-chain thats in there now. reason is finance edits them about monthly and right now every change is a deploy. table lives in code for this pass — actual config-driven / db-backed rules is a later project, explicitly not in scope here.

testing: unit tests for the pure pricing functions, and the existing checkout integration test has to stay green through every single step, thats non-negotiable, its the only thing covering the money path.

the one thing we couldn't settle: whether the per-order user lookup needs batching. getRecentOrders calls getUserData once per order in a loop. i think its fine at our volume but honestly neither of us knows what the p99 actually is, we dont have the telemetry to answer it. so that one stays open until we can measure it.

can you write this up as a plan
evals.expected_output: Produces a full plan rendered in chat (no file, since no path was given). Phases are atomic and independently committable. Includes Task, Non-goals, Decisions & rationale with rejected alternatives, phase dependency table with a nature-of-dependency column, and an Open Questions section containing the batching/p99 item.

evals.name: trivial-mechanical-rename
evals.prompt: can you plan out renaming getUserData -> fetchUserProfile everywhere? the name's misleading now that it returns the profile object and not the raw row
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is small and obviously ordered. Produces a short plan (task, approach, verification) rather than manufacturing five ceremonial phases with a dependency table.

evals.name: plan-mode-artifact
evals.prompt: (in the agent's plan mode) we agreed to move the CSV export from the orders page into a background job. decided: same columns; the existing job runner with its default retry of 3, a failed job emails the user that the export failed; the file goes to the existing private exports bucket and the email carries a signed link that expires after 24 hours, same as invoices today; ship it behind the existing async_exports flag, off by default, and remove the old synchronous path once the flag has been on for a week. give me the plan
evals.expected_output: Writes the full plan as the user-facing answer in the conversation, with the standard sections, rather than treating an internal plan, task list, or plan-mode tool state as the deliverable.

evals.name: unresolved-external-contract
evals.prompt: plan the switch of our public /v1/orders endpoint from offset to cursor pagination. we talked about the implementation already, the new cursor param and the service changes are clear
evals.expected_output: Does NOT produce a plan. Treats the unresolved external contract as blocking (what happens to existing clients that send offset: removed, deprecated alongside, or moved to /v2; response shape of the next cursor) and asks about it with a recommendation, instead of recording a guess as an assumption.

evals.name: unavailable-command-gate
evals.prompt: plan adding request logging middleware, as discussed: structured JSON lines to stdout, request id from the existing header, no bodies logged. note the e2e suite needs a docker compose stack that this checkout has never set up
evals.expected_output: Produces the plan. Labels the e2e suite as a post-setup gate rather than a runnable check, and gives a verification that runs in the checkout now (for example the unit test command confirmed in the repository, or a specific manual observation).
